query: Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr exhibits 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility in the cast state and a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C at strain rates of 10−4–10−2 s−1, but inadequate oxygen resistance prevents most practical high-temperature applications. Earlier oxidation-protection research prevented pesting in a related, non-equiatomic Hf–Nb–Ta–Ti–Zr alloy during a 5 h exposure to air at 800 °C, but that result does not establish protection for equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr; related studies on other refractory alloys likewise did not evaluate this composition. With preservation of useful room- and high-temperature mechanical performance as a design constraint, what single intervention could improve the oxygen resistance of equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr? Formulate one hypothesis identifying the intervention and mechanism, predicting the outcome relative to untreated material, defining the applicable temperature, atmosphere, exposure-time, and loading boundaries, citing supporting evidence from the prior studies, and specifying a controlled experiment and result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Alloying equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr with a small amount of Cr will improve its oxygen resistance by forming a protective oxide layer.
generation.material_initial_state: Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr in the cast state
generation.intervention: Addition of a small amount of Cr
generation.conditions: Exposure to air at temperatures between 800 °C and 1000 °C for up to 5 hours
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of a protective oxide layer
generation.mechanism: The added Cr reacts with oxygen to form a protective Cr2O3 layer, reducing the oxidation rate of the underlying alloy
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved oxygen resistance, as evidenced by reduced oxidation rate and increased resistance to pesting
generation.boundary: Temperature range: 800 °C to 1000 °C, exposure time: up to 5 hours, loading: no external loading
generation.uncertainty: The exact amount of Cr required to achieve optimal oxygen resistance is uncertain and requires further investigation

falsification_experiment.design: Expose untreated and Cr-alloyed equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr samples to air at 900 °C for 2 hours
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the oxidation rate and pesting resistance of the Cr-alloyed sample are not significantly improved compared to the untreated sample, the hypothesis is falsified
